SOAP Clinical Note

Subjective:

- Presenting complaints:
  • Reduced appetite for ~3.5 months  
  • Low energy and “feeling down” for several months  
  • Episodic palpitations and perceived shortness of breath, notably when riding in an elevator  
  • Intermittent headaches and nausea; no vomiting  
  • Unintentional weight loss ≈1 stone (~6 kg) over ~6 months  
- Bowel habits: Normal frequency and form; no diarrhea, blood, or mucus.  
- No chest pain reported.  
- Symptom triggers/relievers: No specific foods precipitate nausea; palpitations occur in elevators, not on routine walking.  
- Past Medical History: Hypothyroidism (under-active thyroid).  
- Medications: Previously on levothyroxine; patient has stopped taking it since changing physician (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
- Social history: 35-year-old male lawyer; job change ~3.5 months ago coincides with appetite decline. No exercise recently.  
- Allergies: Not discussed / not documented.

Objective:

- No physical examination performed during this telehealth visit.  
- Vitals: Not obtained.  
- Investigations/results: None to date.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Fatigue, anorexia, weight loss
   - Assessment: Constitutional symptoms of unclear etiology (rule out anemia, thyroid dysfunction, vitamin deficiency, depression).
   - Investigations planned: Comprehensive blood work (CBC, renal & liver panel, thyroid function tests, vitamin levels).
   - Treatment planned: Await blood results; management will be guided by findings.
   - Follow-up: Patient to arrange phlebotomy via support line; clinician to review results and contact patient.

2. Palpitations / episodic shortness of breath
   - Assessment: Palpitations of uncertain origin (consider anxiety/panic, thyroid abnormality, cardiac arrhythmia).
   - Investigations planned: Included in above bloods; further cardiac evaluation if symptoms worsen or persist.
   - Treatment planned: Education on red-flag symptoms—seek emergency care for chest pain or escalating shortness of breath.

3. Known hypothyroidism, off medication
   - Assessment: Non-adherence to levothyroxine; thyroid status currently unknown.
   - Investigations planned: Thyroid function tests.
   - Treatment planned: Reinstate or adjust levothyroxine based on laboratory results.
   - Follow-up: As above after labs.

Quality checks:

• Missing expected elements: Allergies unasked; complete medication reconciliation incomplete (only levothyroxine discussed).  
• Internal conflicts: Appetite loss began ~3.5 mo ago, weight loss reported over ~6 mo—timeline discrepancy (conflict noted).  
• Transcript quality: Adequate; occasional interruptions but clinically interpretable.
